# Design

Wave 0 gives every later deploy task its two tools: the edge (nginx vhosts, certificates, the internal CA) and the probe (tools/bringup/check-live.sh with one subcommand per system, reading BRINGUP_HOSTS_FILE). Wave 1 makes the kernel real on the kernel host: settlement inputs on the precompiles, the finality verifier bound in layerxd, the bare-host abort points fixed, the genesis and sequencer key generated on the host, systemd units, and a value loop proven through layerxctl. Wave 2 puts the boundaries on the kernel host and the gateway, identity, internal services and registry on the platform host and cuts the Fly endpoint over. Wave 3 completes the human graph for the wallet identity and brings agentd and MCP live. Wave 4 runs in parallel over everything else.

tools/bringup/check-live.sh <subcommand> follows tools/wallet/check-live.sh: one subcommand per system, one line per check printed as pass or fail with the observed value, exit 0 only when every check passes, exit 2 on usage, CHECK_LIVE_TIMEOUT per request; ssh checks use the host map and never print it; tools/bringup/check-live.test.sh exercises the argument parsing and the pass and fail lines against local fixtures.

hosts, ca, edge, kernel-genesis, kernel-node, kernel-value-loop, paxeer-boundary, kernel-boundaries, router, router-cutover, identity, internal, registry, human, agent, human-cutover, wallet, search, archive-node, explorer, developers, relay, interop, mirrors, ramp, gas, bridge, hpx, rpc-nodes

Each host gets /etc/layerx/<service>/env (0600, root) with exactly the env names the pod definition declares, /etc/layerx/<service>/tls with the host-generated key and the CA-signed certificate, and one systemd unit per container named layerx-<service>.service with ExecStart taken from the container command, LoadCredential for every secret file, a dedicated system user matching the pod's uid where one is declared (4020, 4021, 4026, 65532) and Requires or After edges mirroring the pod's init order.
